subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Should exec-approval readers intentionally permit stale-but-coherent snapshots during a current-process write, or must this PR be refactored to a canonical read/write locking contract before merge?
rationale: The patch trades a fail-closed denial for availability inside an authorization boundary; source suggests gateway commits revalidate, but accepting that trade requires owner confirmation that all current and supported callers preserve the same invariant.

options.title: Refactor the read contract
options.body: Define existing-file reads as explicitly lock-free, keep creation and writes serialized, and add caller-level revalidation coverage plus live proof.

options.title: Accept the targeted fallback
options.body: Keep the current exception-based implementation after auditing every synchronous reader and documenting why stale snapshots cannot authorize execution.

recommendation.title: Refactor the read contract
recommendation.body: Define existing-file reads as explicitly lock-free, keep creation and writes serialized, and add caller-level revalidation coverage plus live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this owner to the approval-store locking and gateway failure semantics being changed.
